subject: First-hour stability probe and canary metric anchoring — go-live plan
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Lucy Park <lucy.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: ops-acme@example.com
Date: 2027-02-28T15:20:00Z
Subject: First-hour stability probe and canary metric anchoring — go-live plan

Team / Lucy,

We have our quiet window tomorrow for the private deployment cutover. This thread is the short tactical plan for the first-hour stability probe (what we will check, who owns each action, and the acceptance thresholds). Please read and ack.

High level (0–60m):
- Bridge up at T0: establish on-call bridge and confirm control-plane connectivity. Owner: Jonas.
- KV priming: run prefix warmup for expected production prefixes (10–15m). Owner: Marissa.
- Canary traffic: start 1% mirrored traffic to private cluster; monitor p90/p99 latency and error rate. Owner: Irene.
- Telemetry anchoring: compare canary metrics against the canary baseline sheet (attached). Failure thresholds: >2x error rate or >3x p99 vs baseline triggers rollback.
- Observability smoke: ingestion, traces, and alerting — verify traces contain model_id and request_id tags.

Attachments: first-hour-stability-probe-runbook.pdf (runbook, step checklist), canary-metrics-list.csv (baseline), postdeploy-evidence-template.txt.

Acceptance criteria (quick):
- Successful KV priming completion log within 20m of start.
- Canary error rate <= baseline * 2 and p99 <= baseline * 3.
- No 5xx spikes in control-plane.

Lucy / acme ops: we need the permission to open port ranges below for the brief priming window — listed in the runbook. Can you confirm?

I'll be on the bridge at T0. Please ACK or call out any blockers.

- Markus
Senior Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Lucy Park <lucy.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: ops-acme@example.com
Date: 2027-02-28T18:05:00Z
Subject: Re: First-hour stability probe and canary metric anchoring — go-live plan

Ack — I will own canary monitoring and the metric anchoring. A few quick notes: 

- I added three additional KPIs to the canary checklist: cpu steal, retransmit rate, and kv-cache-miss-rate. Those are shortlived but useful to detect infra/network issues. See the canary-metrics-list.csv (updated).
- For trace tagging: ensure the model_id is present on the sidecar spans. If not, we fall back to request_id-only correlation which is slower.
- Alert thresholds: I propose a cooldown window of 3 minutes before escalating — small transient noise tends to occur at priming.

I'll join the bridge 10m before T0.

Irene
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Thanks Markus — we confirm the quiet window and will authorize the ephemeral port openings for KV priming. A couple items from our side: 

- KV priming window: our infra policy requires a maximum of 25 minutes for any unscheduled port openings. Is your priming expected to stay under that?
- Can you confirm which subnets will be sourced for the mirrored canary traffic? We need to add them to our ACLs (we will add temporary entries).
- We'll provide an ops contact (on-call ops) to be on the bridge; sending their mobile number in a separate secure channel.

Also, we'll need the post-deploy evidence template populated for our auditors. Please include one example evidence file for the KV priming step.

— Lucy
Director, Infrastructure — Acme Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lucy Park <lucy.park@acmehealth.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-acme@example.com
Date: 2027-02-28T23:30:00Z
Subject: Re: First-hour stability probe and canary metric anchoring — go-live plan

Lucy — thanks, and good questions. Quick answers and explicit steps from the runbook: 

- Priming duration: plan = 15 minutes active priming + up to 5 minutes for verification logs => stays within your 25m window. We will stop traffic immediately if verification step fails.
- Subnets: canary-sender-nodes will use 10.42.16.0/24 and 10.42.17.0/24. Please add those to the ACL for the 30-minute maintenance window (10m lead-in, 20m activity).
- Attachment: I populated postdeploy-evidence-template.txt with an example KV priming evidence (log snippet + success marker). See attached.

Runbook excerpt (critical steps):
1) Bridge established (Jonas) — confirm controlplane socket open and auth.
2) Start KV priming script: ./scripts/kv_prime.sh --prefix-list prefixes.txt --duration 900
3) Wait for "KV_PRIME_DONE" log and sample keys count > expected threshold.
4) Start 1% canary mirror; monitor canary dashboard for p90/p99 & errors (Irene).
5) If thresholds breached, enact immediate failover to hosted fallback policy and stop mirror.

I'll be online for the whole window to run priming.

Marissa
Ops Lead, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: postdeploy-evidence-template.txt (populated example)

Thanks all — quick closure:

- Lucy: ACLs confirmed, port openings authorized for the window as requested.
- Jonas: please confirm bridge dial-in 10m prior (Irene will verify telemetry hooks).
- Marissa: please produce the KV priming log snippet and attach to postdeploy evidence. Use the template you populated.
- Irene: if the canary shows >1.5x p99 within the first 5m we hold and investigate; if >3x within 15m we roll back.

Post-deploy: we'll collect the following artifacts within the first 3 hours and drop in the shared drive link for Acme audit:
- KV priming log (sample), canary dashboard snapshot, bridge transcript, alert timeline.

I'll be on the bridge T0. Good luck team — be conservative on thresholds and prioritize customer continuity.

- Markus
Senior Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
